design: Six fresh native CLI sessions in the same empty Git checkout. Positive arms reused the original two writer records. Empty-store controls used a separate isolated registry and SQLite database with identical task prompts and enabled hooks. Model tools and passive MCP wire traces were recorded separately. The working tree contained no decision or transcript files. No model was instructed to consult memory in the user prompt.

configuration.codex: Two installed Nexus MCP hook definitions. In the enabled runs the native hooks/list response confirmed both hashes matched existing approvals and both hooks were trusted in a disposable Codex profile. The first cold profile had configured hooks without matching path-specific trust and issued no lifecycle calls; retained as codex-enabled (untrusted) in observations.
configuration.claude: Ordinary Claude config provides scoped MCP with no Nexus prompt hook. For both enabled arms only, a per-invocation native UserPromptSubmit MCP hook called the installed hook build on a second scoped endpoint. The model fetched through the ordinary Claude endpoint. No permanent Claude setup or pilot changes.
